articles.title: Counter-Strike 2 Pro Aleksib Faces Four-Month Suspended Prison Sentence Over Charges of Aggravated Tax Fraud
articles.summary: Finnish Counter-Strike 2 pro Aleksi “Aleksib” Virolainen is facing a possible four-month suspended prison sentence over alleged “aggravated tax fraud” after failing to declare income from in-game sticker sales.
articles.body:
Finnish Counter-Strike 2 pro Aleksi “Aleksib” Virolainen is facing a possible four-month suspended prison sentence over alleged “aggravated tax fraud” after failing to declare income from in-game sticker sales.

In Counter-Strike 2 , players can purchase virtual stickers and place them on their weapons. They are an in-game item that can be bought on the Steam Marketplace, the CS2 Store, or in capsules, as well as through third-party websites.

It’s not uncommon for professional teams to get a cut of the money earned from sticker sales and other in-game purchases when they compete at major tournaments — and it’s this revenue that prosecutors say Virolainen failed to include on his tax forms.

On Friday, October 16, an indictment was read aloud at the Eastern Uusimaa District Court that accused the pro player of failing to declare €53,000 in income (about $59,553.18 USD) from Valve in 2020, the developer of Counter-Strike 2. Prosecutors claimed that he was able to avoid paying an estimated €28,000 ($31,441 USD) in taxes as a result — but he said he wasn’t aware that this income needed to be declared.

While Virolainen admitted that he failed to declare these earnings, he said that he was just 22 years old at the time with no real understanding of how the tax system worked. The Defense maintained that he was under the impression that his taxes had been fully handled, since taxes had already been taken out of his general income, and that he did not seek any financial gain from failing to report them.

As reported by Finnish news outlet Iltalehti , the alleged offense took place between May 19, 2020 and September 22, 2020 in Vantaa, Finland. A subpoena stated that the player did not return a pre-filled tax return form for the 2019 year and did not report any missing income from Valve.

Prosecutors are demanding that he serve a four-month suspended prison sentence for the alleged offense. Viorlainen has not been formally convicted of the supposed crime, and a district court is set to issue a ruling on the case at a later date.

A tweet containing footage of the pro player arriving at court went viral within the CS2 community, showing him sitting down in the courtroom as cameras flashed in the background. Virolainen reportedly pleaded not guilty to the charges.

The now-29-year-old Aleksib is still an active player, currently representing Natus Vincere. As pointed out by Dexerto , he competed at two Majors with ENCE during the time of the supposed tax fraud, with his most notable finish happening at the IEM Katowice 2019 Major, where his team reached the Grand Finals.

articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters 2 Gets a Theatrical Release After First Movie's Smashing Success on Streaming
articles.summary: The KPop Demon Hunters sequel won’t be repeating the mistakes of its predecessor, having secured a guaranteed theatrical release following the first film’s smashing success.
articles.body:
The KPop Demon Hunters sequel won’t be repeating the mistakes of its predecessor, having secured a guaranteed theatrical release following the first film’s smashing success.

The news was casually and somewhat unceremoniously buried in an October 20 report from The Hollywood Reporter , which dove into the events behind the departure of Netflix’s former film chief, Dan Lin.

According to THR, Lin helped secure a theatrical release for KPop Demon Hunters 2, a move that the outlet noted “hasn’t been officially announced.”

News of a sequel — er, more like sequels — was revealed in November 2025 when Variety reported that Netflix and Sony had inked a deal for a second animated film, with a release date planned for 2029 . Around that same time, The Wrap revealed what’s next for the KPop Demon Hunters universe, including plans for a live-action movie, a stage play and two sequels to create a film trilogy. A spinoff series and short film were also mentioned, though none of these particular projects have been officially announced by the streamer.

Co-director Maggie Kang has already set expectations high for more stories from Huntrix in their quest to protect the Honmoon. “We’ve set up so much for potential backstory,” she told Variety in a July interview. “Obviously, there’s a lot of questions that are left unanswered and areas that are not explored. We had to do that because there’s only so much movie you could tell in 85 minutes.”

KPop Demon Hunters became Netflix’s most-watched offering ever, outperforming live-action films and TV series alike. It spawned oodles of Halloween costumes, sing-along versions of the movie, and oodles of live performances from the film’s singers, EJAE, Rei Ami, and Audrey Nuna ( at the Oscars, no less! ).

The franchise went on to snag collaborations with McDonald’s , Fortnite , and even LEGO , among many others. Given its huge success, it comes as little surprise that Netflix is taking notes from the first film and rolling out the red carpet for its next installment. And considering the popularity of its limited-time theatrical screenings once Netflix took note of its success, it's safe to say that it won't pass up the bag this time around.

Dan Lin was a huge proponent of theatrical releases for Netflix’s films, according to THR’s report. While Co-CEO Ted Sarandos preferred the pandemic-era strategy of going straight to streaming, Lin picked up on the increasing demand for theatrical experiences from younger moviegoers — a footprint he left at the company before his recent exit.

In related news, Derpy the tiger recently scored a 37,000-Piece Kpop Demon Hunters Build with LEGO — a far funner story than a Christian metal band called Demon Hunter that sued Netflix over copyright infringement earlier this year. (Netflix dismissed these claims, saying the “allegations are without merit” in an official statement.)

articles.title: Cooking Up Magick Kicks Off a New Fantasy Romance Series Hints of The Lord of the Rings Sprinkled In
articles.body:
The first book in a new series called The Dell Chronicles, HL Bernabe’s Cooking Up Magick sets out to be a cozier fantasy version of The Lord of the Rings . And in many ways, it does pull directly from J.R.R. Tolkien’s world. The main character, Paisley, is a halfling who gets swept up on an adventure with a pair of dwarves, but unbeknownst to her, there’s also an evil overlord that has just returned after centuries – and she’s the only hope the world has to actually stop him.

The similarities to The Hobbit and LOTR pretty much end there though, and you don’t get nearly enough detail in the first book to effectively flesh out this alternate version of Middle-earth. What you do get is a lovable main character who is surrounded by an interesting cast of characters. There’s cooking, there’s magic, and there’s even a bit of romantasy thrown in here, but Cooking Up Magick doesn’t serve up enough of any of it to fully bring its story to life.

Cooking Up Magick: The Dell Chronicles Book One

Cooking Up Magick shines brightest whenever the core characters are interacting with each other. Paisley is a bubbly bright spot among the crew, capable of immense courage and compassion. She has a sort of magnetism that rubs off on her friends and which helps shine a light on each of their individual personalities. Her conversations and moments with her newfound friends (and her Half-Orc love interest) really help to ground the story’s core concept of found family.

Naturally, these moments are often centered around the idea of cooking or magic. Paisley’s driving reason for leaving her home and her family’s inn is that she wants to discover new and exciting recipes to eventually bring back. Her sense of adventure is entirely tied to the idea of roaming the world and dipping her toes in the culinary culture it has to offer. But that core motivation quickly fades to the background as larger events start to unfold. There are flashes where cooking comes to the forefront of the story, but it rarely feels like food actually matters beyond an initial plot driver and a reason for the characters to come together.

As someone who is always happy to geek out about cooking, I expected the author to showcase more of that in Paisley's character. It’s clear that she likes it, sure, but the writing seems to spend too much time telling us that and not enough time showing it. Going into this book, I had hoped to see Delicious in Dungeon -levels of enthusiasm for cooking and found myself a bit disappointed that it wasn’t what I got.

So while Paisley’s personality doesn’t necessarily shine through her cooking, we do get a better feeling for it through her magical ability. She doesn’t discover her powers until the story progresses a bit, but once they start to manifest, they show up in ways you’d expect from a compassionate chef. She’s able to draw power from her love of her companions and spread that to the world around her. With this power, she’s able to heal, protect, and even connect on a deeper level with her friends. But once she gains her magic, cooking pretty much takes a backseat for the story, and sure, seeing as she’s the first new sorcerer in this world in a really long time, it definitely makes sense for this to take over the story. As she learns about her new powers, so do we, and it’s some of the best Paisley character building we get in the entire story.

Beyond the core characters, much of the book is driven by Verzod, the evil sorcerer. He’s the one who’s inciting war in an otherwise peaceful land, and acts as the obvious antagonist to Paisley (and everyone else). Despite getting multiple chapters from his perspective, it’s hard to draw any other conclusions about him beyond his just being the pure embodiment of evil. The only character depth we’re really able to glean is his soft spot for his lost talking cat, Whipclaw. But since said cat spends most of the book with Paisley, we don’t really get to explore that side of him. I would have much preferred to have left him as a mysterious outside entity that gets revealed in later books, but there’s still plenty of room to flesh out his motives later on. As is, his existence serves its purpose as the inciting action of the story.

articles.title: Marvel's VisionQuest Series Gets Better in Episodes 3 and 4, as Paul Bettany's Hero Begins to Get in Touch With His Humanity
articles.summary: VisionQuest improves in Episodes 3 and 4, as Paul Bettany's White Vision begins to make strides in recapturing his missing humanity.
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for VisionQuest Episodes 3 and 4, which are streaming now on Disney+.

VisionQuest is turning out to be quite the pleasant little surprise. What initially seemed like an obligatory but unneeded follow-up to a loose end from WandaVision is rapidly developing into a series with plenty of heart, soul, and depth of its own. It never pays to count out Paul Bettany's synthetic hero.

Mind you, entertaining as the first two episodes were, my one real reservation with VisionQuest out of the gate was that it was a bit difficult to connect with this version of Bettany's character. As he himself says, he has all the memories of the original Vision but none of his soul. Given how poignant and utterly human Vision was in his past MCU appearances, seeing a cold, aloof, emotionless copy of that character takes some getting used to.

But that problem quickly starts to fade in Episodes 3 and 4. Already, White Vision is making great strides in terms of understanding his emotions and internal conflict and embracing this side of himself he doesn't quite understand. Compared to the Loki series , which basically relied on a quick-and-dirty speedrun to transform the 2012-era Loki (Tom Hiddleston) into something more resembling his post- Thor: Ragnarok self, this feels like a more coherent and purposeful way of bridging the gap between two wildly different versions of an MCU character.

Certainly, Bettany has a lot more to work with in these two episodes, both comedically and dramatically. His malfunctioning processors give the actor some welcome opportunity to deploy a bit of physical comedy in Episode 3. And both episodes make the most of the rapidly deepening bond between Vision and Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica). By all rights, their relationship should feel rushed, but somehow it all works anyway. By the time Vision is coaxing his son on how to reboot him in the hotel swimming pool, he feels well on the road to reclaiming that lost humanity that was so vital to the original character. That process continues in Episode 4, where Vision pointedly stops drawing such a hard distinction between his past and present selves.

I also appreciate how well the show's writers are succeeding in not making Agatha All Along required viewing. This isn't a show you want to watch without at least having seen WandaVision, but it also does a fine job of explaining everything you need to know about Tommy's bizarre existence without making his brother Billy's (Joe Locke) parallel journey into mandatory homework. It helps the series stand on its own two feet a bit more, rather than simply being the final act of a trilogy.

Another big plus in VisionQuest's favor is that it features such a lovable supporting cast of AI goofballs. James Spader's Ultron doesn't steal the show to quite the degree he did in the first two episodes, but he remains one of the absolute highlights of the series. Ultron is great for both periodic comedic relief and the sorts of knowing observations on human nature that used to be Vision's purview. But we also get to see the character finally take a more purposeful step onto center stage late in Episode 4, as he manipulates his way into taking the wheel (literally) and predictably betrays his family at his first opportunity. The prospect of an Ultron fully in control and back in the physical world is a very exciting one heading into Episode 5.

Speaking of Vision's family, we get a lot of great scenes involving F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Orla Brady), E.D.I.T.H. (Emily Hampshire), and even D.U.M.-E. (Henry Lewis) and U (Jonathan Sayer). The series is doing a fantastic job of fleshing out and enriching these characters that used to be nothing more than disembodied voices or slapstick workshop tools. Episode 4 is particularly strong when it comes to exploring their own emotional journeys and how much they parallel what Vision is experiencing.

None of this is to say the series isn't still experiencing some growing pains. Episodes 3 and 4 feel a bit clunky in how they handle the transition from a conflict mostly built around Paladin (Todd Stashwick) to one centered around Jocasta (T'Nia Miller). The former character basically drops out of the picture after running afoul of the latter. Still, I'm enjoying the show's take on Jocasta so far. She's nothing if not sympathetic so far, and she holds a lot of potential as both a villain and the object of Ultron's fascination. All in all, these two episodes do a lot to set up a compelling conflict for the second half of the series.

articles.title: Sony Issues New PS5 Firmware Update as Jailbreak Race Heats Up Ahead of GTA 6 Release
articles.summary: Sony has issued a new PlayStation 5 firmware update amid the homebrew community's ongoing effort to jailbreak the console.
articles.body:
Sony has issued a new PlayStation 5 firmware update amid the homebrew community's ongoing effort to jailbreak the console.

PS5 system software update 26.07-14.20.00 is available now and weighs in at 1.2 GB. While Sony’s official patch notes suggest its only function is to improve “the messages and usability on some screens,” some believe it may perform other functions under the hood.

PS5 firmware update 26.07-14.20.00 patch notes:

We've improved the messages and usability on some screens.

The PlayStation homebrew scene hit the headlines in recent weeks for releasing PS5 jailbreaks for prior firmwares. For example, late last month, a jailbreak that supported all PS5 consoles running firmware 7.00-13.60 sent shockwaves through the homebrew community. At the time, it meant that all PS5s, including the PS5 Pro, that hadn't been updated within the previous week, were compatible with the jailbreak.

This is of huge significance for Sony and the security of the PS5, as people with a jailbroken PS5 can modify their console, potentially opening the door to video game piracy. However, it was found that some PS5 games subsequently required the latest 14.00 firmware in order to download updates, sparking a renewed effort to release a new jailbreak for the updated system software.

So, there is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security. It’s worth pointing out that Sony makes no mention of security in today’s patch notes.

This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, which comes out in less than a month, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.

One prominent member of the PlayStation homebrew community recently showed evidence of a jailbreak for the 14.10 firmware, but follow up comments suggest that dumping game executables isn't possible. There is no evidence to suggest that today’s 14.20 update is a response to that. However, some believe GTA 6 will require at least 14.20 to run, now it’s out in the wild. Sony may even release a further security update before November 19.

The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for Sony, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly.

articles.title: 'Aragorn Will Always Be Viggo,' Says Jamie Dornan Ahead of His Turn as the Iconic Character in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum
articles.summary: Jamie Dornan will play a younger Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, but he’s aware of the magnitude of his role, and doesn’t see his take on the character as a replacement for Viggo Mortensen.
articles.body:
Jamie Dornan will play a younger Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum , but he’s aware of the magnitude of his role, and doesn’t see his take on the character as a replacement for Viggo Mortensen.

"There's pressure when you're trying to follow in those footsteps," Dornan told ScreenRant . "I've been asked to play a super-iconic role, and I'll do my best.

“But for me, Aragorn will always be just Viggo. His performance is one of my all-time favorites, and I feel honored to try to recapture at least some of the energy he originally brought to the character. There's no part of me that's trying to outdo him."

The Lord of the Rings Movies in (Chronological) Order

Northern Ireland actor Dornan is best known for his leading role in Fifty Shades of Grey. Viggo Mortensen has already gone on record to back the casting choice, saying he was “thrilled.”

The Hunt for Gollum takes place between The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings and follows Gandalf and Aragorn as they track Sméagol across Middle-earth to find out if a certain magical ring is Sauron's One Ring. The story is summarized in Tolkien’s The Fellowship of the Ring novel, but the movie will build upon those short passages and flesh the journey out into a full story.

Dornan is joined by Leo Woodall (White Lotus, One Day), who will play a fellow Dúnedain Ranger called Halvard joining Strider on his mission. Lee Pace will also return to his Hobbit trilogy role as Thranduil the Elvenking.

Andy Serkis returns as Gollum and also directs the movie, while Sir Ian McKellen and Elijah Wood reprise their classic roles as Gandalf and Frodo respectively. Mortensen previously said he’d only return as Aragorn if he “was right for the character.”

The actor also previously spoke about how he “wasn’t crazy about” the digital de-ageing technology used in The Irishman, which could potentially be a reason he won’t don the cloak and hood again. Of course, we haven’t seen what technology The Hunt for Golem uses to make Elijah Wood and Sir Ian McKellen look younger than they did in the original trilogy yet, with set pictures only showing us a glimpse of Frodo’s back .

Filming began earlier this year, and was teased with photos of Serkis squatting in the motion capture volume , getting his Gollum on. Rather his knees than mine. Elsewhere, Peter Jackson has confirmed The Lord of the Rings: Shadow of the Past is in the scriptwriting stage following cancellation rumors that emerged in the wake of the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.

articles.title: CD Projekt's Cyberpunk 2077 Loremaster Confirms Year Edgerunners 2 Is Set, Sparking Fan Speculation About Canon Endings
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red loremaster Patrick Mills has revealed the exact year Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 takes place, amid speculation from fans about what it means for the ending of Cyberpunk 2077.
articles.body:
CD Projekt Red loremaster Patrick Mills has revealed the exact year Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 takes place, amid speculation from fans about what it means for the ending of Cyberpunk 2077.

According to Mills, Season 2 takes place not long after you bite the bullet and finally meet Hanako at Embers in Cyberpunk 2077.

"Ok so the thing is that I am seeing a lot of people assuming S2 takes place before 2077 but it doesn't, it takes place in 2078," Mills confirmed in a post on Bluesky . "Moving things forward, time doesn't stop in Cyberpunk."

Mills previously posted about a misunderstanding he had seen in early reviews of the series, but wanted to wait until it was out before dropping a truth nuke.

In Edgerunners Season 2, powerful corporation Arasaka doesn’t quite have the same pull it did during the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , which is a hint that the anime takes place after the events of the game. There are also some other smaller and bigger details, but like the loremaster, I don’t want to spoil things for you.

Now they know Edgerunners 2 is set just a year after the events of Cyberpunk 2077, fans are trying to work out what it means for the plot of the game . Some believe it suggests certain endings are canon. Or, perhaps it would be better to say, some believe it suggests certain endings are not canon. In truth, Edgerunners 2 doesn't force CD Projekt into making a decision about canon — a bit like Bethesda's position on Fallout canon in the context of the Amazon TV show, which takes place after all the video games.

The world of Cyberpunk is set to expand further, of course, with the in-development Cyberpunk 2 (where and when the game takes place is yet to be announced). There's also a live-action film in the works, although according to CD Projekt, the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't retrace the game's steps .

Before all that, Cyberpunk 2077 is set for a surprise Edgerunners 2-themed update this week. CD Projekt has confirmed it features cyberware customization and a new dual-wielding playstyle. CDPR released a similar update to tie into the first season. The Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners update added a short questline that let players track down the cool yellow jacket the protagonist of Season 1 wore. There’s a good chance the new update will come with some similar surprises when it drops on October 22.

More details about the Edgerunners 2 update will be revealed today, October 21, 2026, during a special episode of REDstreams.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra Australia Launch: Everything You Need to Know, Specs and Local Pricing
articles.body:
Take note of the following, my fellow fans of fine tech (and maybe take that note with a generously included S Pen). Samsung’s Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra launches in Australia on 22 October 2026, starting at $2,299. Its headline features include a 14.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display, a MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, an 11,600mAh battery and the aforementioned S Pen. Samsung is also bundling software offers advertised at more than $539 in combined value, making the tablet worth a closer look for anyone considering a premium device for work, study or creative projects.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is built around a mighty simple idea: give folks plenty of screen real estate and software flexibility to tackle several jobs, thus removing the need to go full octopus and constantly reach for other devices. Its remarkably thin design helps make this large display solution more portable, while multitasking tools and AI features broaden its appeal beyond streaming and browsing.

Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra: Australian price and specifications

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra will be available in Australia from 22 October in Grey, with Wi-Fi and 5G configurations.

Please refer to Samsung.com.au for full product and feature details, terms and conditions.

The starting price covers the entry configuration, with higher storage options available for people who wish to squirrel away larger collections of media, games or creative projects on the tablet. You can even super-size and use the microSD card slot to expand storage, too.

See Samsung Australia's Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra page for local purchasing details.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra’s defining feature is its 14.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display. With a 120Hz refresh rate, 2960 x 1848 resolution and advertised peak brightness of 1,600 nits, the screen is designed for everything from detailed creative work to high-definition entertainment.

Samsung’s Vision Booster technology adjusts the display’s brightness and contrast to suit surrounding lighting conditions. That should be particularly useful when moving between indoor workspaces and brighter environments.

Despite the generous screen dimensions, the tablet measures just 5.1mm thick and weighs 692g in its Wi-Fi configuration. The large display gives users room to keep multiple applications visible, while the slim chassis makes the device easier to slip into a bag between meetings, classes or trips.

An 11,600mAh battery is rated for up to 23 hours of video playback under Samsung’s stated conditions. The tablet supports 45W charging, although the charging adapter is sold separately. Its also been tested to IP68 lab test standards.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra runs Android 17 with Samsung’s One UI 9 interface, bringing Galaxy AI features and multitasking tools into the same workspace.

Multi Window supports three simultaneous app views. That means users can follow an online tutorial, take notes and consult reference material without repeatedly switching between applications. Note Assist can help summarise and organise information, while Gemini provides AI assistance for research and everyday tasks.

Gemini Notebook offers another way to organise material, bringing together information and helping users work through their notes and reference content. Together, these tools are intended to make the tablet useful for more involved tasks, rather than simply providing a larger surface for mobile apps.

Samsung DeX adds a desktop-style interface with a taskbar, resizable windows and drag-and-drop support. Combined with an optional keyboard accessory, it provides another way to approach document work and multitasking. As to whether it can replace a laptop, I reckon that’ll depend on the applications and workflows involved. But it sure seems viable, generally speaking.

Alternatively, if productivity is the very last thing on your mind, the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra features powerful internal components tailored for high-end mobile gaming. Driven by the 3nm MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, it effortlessly runs demanding titles like Genshin Impact at a smooth 60 frames per second.

Up to 16GB of LPDDR5X RAM prevents background lag, while an advanced 3D vapor chamber ensures excellent thermal management during extended play. Backed by that expansive 14.6-inch 120Hz Dynamic AMOLED 2X display and a massive 11,600mAh battery, what’s here should deliver the sustained power needed for an immersive, top-tier portable gaming setup.

S Pen, Photoshop and more than $539 in included value

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra includes an S Pen in the box, valued at $129 in Samsung’s offer breakdown. The stylus supports handwriting, annotation and drawing without requiring a separate purchase.

Eligible new devices also qualify for a collection of software offers with a combined advertised value of $539.90:

● Google AI Pro : Six months, valued at $197.94.

● Adobe Photoshop premium access : Four months, valued at $143.96.

● Notability Plus : Six-month trial, valued at $69.

Photoshop provides image-editing tools, including AI-assisted features, while Notability offers multimedia note-taking, audio synchronisation, transcription and handwriting conversion. Those additions are particularly relevant to users who plan to create, annotate or organise information on the tablet.

Pro tip: The advertised value isn't equivalent to a permanent cash saving. Eligibility and redemption requirements apply, some offers are limited to new subscribers, and subscription charges may apply after promotional periods unless cancelled. So best you check the terms before activating each offer.

Where to buy the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra in Australia

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra launches in Australia on 22 October 2026, from $2,299. It will be available in Grey through Samsung Australia's, as well as retailers: Amazon, JB Hi-Fi, The Good Guys, Harvey Norman, Bing Lee, Officeworks and Costco, and carriers: Telstra, Optus and Vodafone.

For buyers who need a large display, stylus input and flexible multitasking in a slim tablet, the specification sheet gives plenty to consider. I’d say the key decision is how much use you'll make of those productivity and creative features, particularly at this price. Personally, it’s making a lot of sense to me right now.

Visit Samsung Australia for local availability and configuration details.

articles.title: Nvidia’s latest GPU driver brings a new way to speed up PC games
articles.summary: Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology is now part of Nvidia’s drivers.
articles.body: Nvidia is rolling out a new GPU driver today (621.01) that enables Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology to speed up game launches. The technology also removes mid-game “just-in-time” shader compilation, reducing stuttering and CPU spikes. Microsoft’s Advanced Shader Delivery works by offloading shader compilation for different hardware combinations to the cloud. “Using DirectX 12, Windows 11, and the Microsoft Agility SDK, developers capture shaders into a State Object Database (SODB), allowing Microsoft’s cloud network to precompile shaders for hundreds of thousands of hardware and driver combinations,” explains Nvidia’s Andrew Burnes. Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 now both support Advanced Shader Delivery, as long as you download the games via the Xbox PC app. “This system is storefront-agnostic, meaning you benefit even when playing games purchased on Steam, as long as the Xbox PC app is installed on your PC,” says Burnes. Advanced Shader Delivery will let you skip the annoying shader compilation screen in Call of Duty, and it should improve the overall performance of supported games. “With a near-100 percent cache hit rate, it eliminates mid-game ‘just-in-time’ shader compilation, wiping out CPU spikes and frame stutters in titles like Gears of War: E-Day, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. You can download Nvidia’s latest 621.01 update here, and Advanced Shader Delivery is also supported on AMD GPUs with Adrenalin 26.6.1 or higher and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 series with driver version 2026.08.3 or higher.
